hook: Daphne Koller earned undergraduate and masters degrees in computer science from the Hebrew University of Jerusalem before completing a PhD in computer science at Stanford University in 1993. She joined the Stanford faculty in 1995 and spent nearly two decades there as the Rajeev Motwani Professor of Computer Science, building a research program in probabilistic graphical models, a framework for reasoning under uncertainty that she detailed with Nir Friedman in the widely used textbook Probabilistic Graphical Models, Principles and Techniques. In 2012 she co-founded Coursera with fellow Stanford professor Andrew Ng, serving as co-CEO and president as the platform grew into one of the largest providers of massive open online courses. She later served as chief computing officer at Calico, an Alphabet company focused on aging research, before founding insitro in 2018, where she is CEO and applies machine learning and large scale biological data to drug discovery and development.
